verdict.tagline: Gorgeous open-world racing hampered by intrusive ads and account hurdles.
for_you_if: you want expansive open-world racing environments
you enjoy immediate access to high-end supercars
not_for_you_if: you will not link a Microsoft account
you need a structured career progression from slow cars
you want clean multiplayer matchmaking without ramming

distortion_flags.sentence: Initial reviews skew heavily negative due to account login hurdles and promotional interruptions, while reviews from later play trend overwhelmingly positive.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe frequent interruptions from advertisements and pop-up prompts to buy DLCs, upgrades, or newer versions of the game during early play.

citations.review_text: I could not get pass the cringe and the constantly asking me to buy stuff and upgrade my game 3.5/10

I wanted to play with friends. Trying to match up to play together is an absolute pain. The ingame friendslist seems effectively nonfunctional. Even on Windows friends cannot join up together unless they have XBOX Gamebar installed or use a mobile companion app. I can neither invite nor join others, as I'm playing on Linux. XBOX Gamebar allows inviting, joining and accepting invites but without it or the companion app, Windows users also couldnt join e/o. Even being invited by friends with XBOX Gamebar didnt work for me. I'd receive the invites only on the XBOX website, where I could not accept them. Ingame no invites popped up. 

That kind of functionality (or lack thereof rather) is unacceptable for a product of this caliber imho. Thus, refund. A shame because the game in and off itself seems fun and yes I can see solo play is a blast, performance seemed fine. But this experience soured me on it significantly.

Theres ofc also the advertisements. Gameplay gets (not totally abruptly but still) interrupted by full on advertisement spots for other Forza products regularly. Theyre always followed by purchase banners. In my <100 mins of playtime I got 3 advertisement spots. 

A side note I could have lived with and obvsly is down to me not being on a supported distro: While the game is running for me (FEDORA 44 KDE), all other open windows become nonfunctional. Did not try to troubleshoot this, see above.

Absolutely not. 
My game was interrupted twice in the span of an hour to ask if I wanted to buy FH6 and then if I wanted to upgrade to Premium. Garbage marketing director—it would take 129.99 Euros to turn this comment into a positive one.
Besides the above, there were problems with the activation of the Microsoft account, which required 30 minutes to sort out... because reasons... MicroSlop, get better leadership and pay them less.

Driving is fun enough, even though the constant chatter is a bit obnoxious, but I don't like extra logins for my single player experiences. Neither do I enjoy full screen ads for the sequel in the middle of my game. You can shove those where the sun doesn't shine. Same goes for lengthy unskippable cutscenes. Also, the game won't even start while Process Explorer is running in the background? Are you f*cking insane? Uninstalled. Refunded.

Some minutes in you get to choose between some very racist avatars with hair and handicaps as only customisation. Men only get to choose between some 15 womens hairstyles. Or be shaved. I drive for five minutes to some spot in the road, hit X and is hit with ANOTHER unskippable cutscene. Then it wants me to pay more money.

This is when I just deleted the game and sent a refund request.

I don't have to look at my woke avatar, so I saw through that. But I have limits.

I did not enjoy this Forza game. I felt like the tutorial never ended. To be honest I not sure it does. The likes are that when you don't have to deal with the cliche characters The vehicle models are well-detailed. The landscapes are eh, standard for many open-world games set in Mexico, and the driving controls handle well. 
The major dislikes are the forced content of the intro and annoying mandatory cliche dialogue. Human designs are awful to look at, which exist far more frequently than I'd expect in a Forza based game. The dialogue is so freaking boring and drawn out. Blah, blah, blah <unthought out generic Latino cliche phrasing> blah, blah <just like somewhere random expositional/backstory no one cares about>  blah, blah, blah. Unfortunately the dialogue is not creative nor enjoyable and robs the player of what could be a great rally/racing simulator in an otherwise beautiful game. 
I could not find enjoyment for this game as the into feels more purposeless than Skyrim's and pointless other than to say "hey look at the colorful plane"
If you can live with the dislikes, cool it likely will not be a bad game. If you hate unneeded dialogue and pointless gimmicks I would not recommend as these are very present and highly distracting; breaking a true immersion.

citations.review_text: Erm, its good at first but becomes to samey, not enough mods for the cars imo.

Honestly one of the best racing games I've played. The graphics are beautiful, the car selection is insane and there's just so much to do. Driving around Mexico, exploring the map, racing or just cruising with friends never gets boring. The amount of customization is also amazing.

The only downside is that progression can get a little repetitive after a while, but overall it's an amazing experience.

Forza Horizon 5 is not a bad game, but still impossible to recommend due to the following issues:
- no sense of progression
- mind-numbingly boring and childish story (you can evade this point by turning the voice volume all the way down)
- unskippable cutscenes
- physics engine is poor
- in-game ads
- solid 5 minutes loading screen to start up the game
- it is basically copy paste of Forza Horizon 4; but the copy is worse

Get it on sale but I wouldn’t recommend it at 60€

For me, this was the first arcade racing game I've played in a long time, and I really enjoyed my time with it. I found the variety of scenery to be its main selling point—being able to drive in an open world featuring snow, beaches, jungles, temples, and a volcano was quite unique.

It's interesting that there are also plenty of advanced tuning options for experienced players, allowing you to fine-tune and test controls so the car feels exactly how you want. The stories were nice, and I liked that they squeezed a bit of local and automotive history into some of the story quests.

Things I didn't enjoy as much: I wasn't a fan of the story progression. When you start the game, you're given five car classes that are already top-tier, and you're immediately known as the best racer—which makes you wonder, what's the motivation to compete? Also, the map layout: trying to find the next story chapter after finishing one was quite frustrating.
Another thing I did not like was: If you got distracted by another event (which you often do to earn some cash), your current waypoint disappears, forcing you to dig through a dense wall of map markers just to find where the story continues. As a newcomer to the series, I found map navigation and waypoint tracking very annoying. At least there were some filters I could add to remove the clutter. 

That said, I really enjoyed the time I spent with the game. Having finished all the single-player stories (though not all with 3 stars), all Exhibition events, and all the final showcase races, I genuinely enjoyed almost every minute of it

Definitely one of the best racing games I've ever played. There's a massive variety of cars, and getting your hands on them is pretty easy. The story is also surprisingly good. The Horizon Adventure missions are awesome, and the side quests are just as fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game hands out expensive supercars and high-end vehicles very early, which diminishes the sense of progression and makes expensive cars feel unearned.

citations.review_text:
This game gives you a Lamborghini for completing the tutorial, a Ferrari for sneezing, and another supercar because you opened the menu.

Welcome to Mexico, where apparently everyone is a millionaire.

Forza Horizon 5 is a fantastic open-world racer. The driving feels amazing, Mexico looks gorgeous, and the sheer variety of cars, races, and activities can keep you busy for hundreds of hours.

Unfortunately, progression feels almost meaningless when expensive cars are handed out like supermarket coupons. The festival dialogue is painfully enthusiastic, the story is forgettable, and online features can occasionally test your patience.

The Good:

Excellent arcade driving and car variety.

Stunning visuals and diverse environments.

Tons of races, customization, and freedom.

The Bad:

Progression is way too generous.

Forgettable story and excessive festival chatter.

Repetitive activities and occasional online frustrations.

Ratings:

Gameplay: 9/10

Graphics: 9.5/10

Content & Variety: 9/10

Progression: 6/10

Enjoyment: 9/10

Overall: 8.5/10 | Recommended

One of the best arcade racing experiences around. Just don't expect to feel rich when the game treats a Bugatti like a participation trophy.

Honestly an amazing game. There is just so much to do. Both the Hot Wheels and Rally Adventure expansions are super unique and worth diving into. In my opinion, the Premium Edition is totally worth the price. The only real caveat is that it drops a ton of high end cars into your garage right away. It takes away a bit of the early game grind and progression, but being able to fly across Mexico in hyper cars from the very start is hard to complain about.

citations.review_text: Weeklies are a nightmare, 3min of waiting to even start seatching for a lobby, then searching time (sometimes even 10min) to get a moron who crashes after 10sec and ruins your game so you have to repeat the whole process again... Why the fuck do I have to wait 3min for a fucking match making to start working?! Doshit design. Also menus are cancer, everything takes 10 times longer than it should. This game doesn't respect your time on so many levels that i can't recommend it to anyone. A lot of cars are in paid dlcs that don't even come with the most expensive edition.  Driving model of faster cars is ass and there are a lot of smaller issues. Racing is weak, exploration is good so is graphics and car selection but that's about it.

Honestly... don't waste your money unless its on sale or something.  The driving is very slide-y, and the physics are a bit odd.  Sure its not bad for an arcade style game.  Honestly though, after playing for a bit, i just find it to be more boring to play.  Plus, playing online is a no-go of someone using you as a brake system and keeping you at the back of the race.  Why in the world other actual player drivers can hit me during races is just plain aggravation.  There's lots to explore and a ton of races, but once you explore the map it just gets dull.  Not being able to talk to people in the game is just something that bewilders me.  To think they thought people wanted to farm for 'permission to speak using catchphrases' is beyond me.  Maybe if this game had a multiplayer presence, it would be a lot better.  Honestly though, the most you get from other people in the game is a drag race at the strip, or people that just want to drive around the map aimlessly.  The lack of the ability to communicate with other people makes other players in the game feel more like well done AI than another player.  The entire game just feels like its lacking in every aspect in some way or another.  Just boring.  Plus.. to top it all off, Microslop lol.  That should be all you need to know about this game.
